where: Section 1, coverage formula and Section 3, redundant faults
problem: The chapter defines fault coverage as detected faults divided by the testable fault list. Most standard textbooks define fault coverage as detected faults divided by the total collapsed fault list (redundant faults included), and call detected ÷ testable 'fault efficiency' (or 'test efficiency'). A student who writes the chapter's formula in an exam that uses the textbook definition loses marks.
fix: Keep the chapter formula but add one line: C = N_detected ÷ N_testable × 100% is called fault efficiency in some books; the plain 'fault coverage' used by other books divides by the whole collapsed list, redundant faults included. State that the chapter uses the testable-list version so 100 % stays reachable.

problem: Packing '32 or 64 faults into the bits of a machine word' is slightly off. In parallel fault simulation one bit of the word is reserved for the good circuit, so a 32-bit word carries the good circuit plus 31 faulty copies, not 32 faults.
fix: Say 'a w-bit word holds the good circuit in one bit and w − 1 faulty copies in the rest, so a 32-bit word simulates 31 faults at a time'.

problem: The split between a redundant fault and an 'untestable fault' is muddled. Standard texts treat the two as the same thing: a fault with no test is redundant (undetectable). The examples given, a tied-off input and a blocked path, are themselves causes of redundancy, not a separate category.
fix: Write: 'A redundant (untestable, undetectable) fault has no test. Common causes: the fault is masked by the logic, an input is tied to a constant, or every path to an output is blocked. Such faults are excluded from the coverage denominator.'

problem: The question asks the student to show the D-frontier, but the step headed 'D-frontier' jumps straight into propagation through Z and never states the set. After steps 2 and 3 the D-frontier is exactly {Z}, and the student must say so to earn the mark.
fix: Begin step 4 with: 'After step 3 the only gate with D-bar on an input and no D on its output is Z, so the D-frontier is {Z}.' Then propagate through Z as shown.

problem: The last clause, 'so an all-fault target may be below 100 %', reads backwards and will confuse a reader.
fix: Say: '100 % coverage of all faults may be impossible, because redundant faults are never detected; 100 % of the testable list can be less than 100 % of the full fault list.'
